market_summary: Wall Street rallied Wed (S&P +1.31%, Nasdaq +1.60%, Dow +0.49%) as chips led after CoreWeave's beat, with bonds shut for Veterans Day and a December Fed hike near fully priced after hot October CPI. Then Nvidia fell about 8% after hours on reports its board met late Wednesday to decide whether to oust Jensen Huang; no decision is reported yet. Asia held up better than feared on Thursday: Nikkei roughly flat to +0.5%, Kospi flat, Taiwan -1.2%, ASX 200 -0.4% to 9,117, Hong Kong a drag on the region. US futures are lower (Nasdaq 100 about -0.9%, S&P 500 about -0.4%), and oil eased (Brent about $92, WTI about $86). The AI capex trade now faces Nvidia's leadership question, its Nov 17 results, and Anthropic's IPO pricing on Nov 18 at a $70-78 range.

MRVL.reason: Up 9.3% in the chip rebound after CoreWeave results; still recovering from a 13% drop on the Lumentum deal.

MU.reason: Up 11.9% on CoreWeave results and a $1B Anthropic IPO allocation; still about 35% below its 52-week high.

NVDA.reason: Up 2.9% in session, then about 8% lower after hours on WSJ report the board may oust Huang; no successor named.

OPENAI.reason: March 2026 round at $852B post-money vs $157B in Oct 2024, about 5.4x; no newer round found. Source: pymnts.com.

headlines: Nvidia down over 7% after hours: WSJ says the board is preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang; decision pending.
Wall St rose Wed: S&P +1.3%, Nasdaq +1.6%; chips led after CoreWeave, Micron +11.9%, Marvell +9.3%.
Anthropic IPO reported several times oversubscribed at $70-78; prices Nov 18, trades as ANT Nov 19 (Fri AEDT).
Asia softer Thu: Taiwan -1.2%, ASX -0.4%; Nasdaq futures about -0.9%.
Next: Figure Q3 before open and Cisco, AMAT after close (Fri morning AEDT); PPI Fri.
